newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Koncar sees privatisation this year.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Koncar sees privatisation this year.

text.p: Croatian electrical giant Koncar, in which Germany's Siemens has a small stake, said on Tuesday it hoped to be privatised by the end of this year.
"We are preparing the process which is long and quite complex, but we expect it to be over towards the end of 1997," Koncar president Vjekoslav Srb told a news conference.
Although the privatisation method is still to be determined by the Croatian government, Srb said Koncar would probably follow in the steps of drugs firm Pliva.

Some 30 percent of Pliva's stock was floated at home and abroad in March 1996 via Union Bank of Switzerland and Croatian Zagrebacka Banka. The company was later listed on the London and Zagreb stock exchanges.
Koncar said in November 1996 its development plans to year 2000 envisaged a listing in Croatia and on a foreign bourse.
Economy Minister Davor Stern, who also attended the news conference, denied rumours that any firm had been put in charge of Koncar's eventual issue.
But he said there were "several foreign candidates".
Through its privatisation agency and two pension funds the government controls over 60 percent of the company, whose capital is estimated at roughly 365 million German marks.
Croatia also plans to offer shares in state-owned Janaf, the Adriatic pipeline operator, later this year. The issue will be led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
